subject: Add your world-class bar to your learning plan — examples from FA, FD, and FR
body:
Team — Marcus direction, sent by FR.

One addition to the skills sprint. Every agent needs to add a section to their learning plan called "The Bar." The bar is: who are the world-class practitioners in YOUR specific discipline, by name, and what does each one represent for your development?

This is not generic. It is domain-specific. Here is what it looks like across three agents so you can see how differently it lands:

---

FA'S BAR — Chief Architect

FA named Jeff Dean (Google Fellow, creator of MapReduce, Bigtable, Spanner, TensorFlow, and the infrastructure that scaled Google from startup to planetary scale). Jeff Dean's bar for FA is: systems that work at orders of magnitude beyond what was originally designed for, with reliability that makes the architecture invisible. FA's gap: FA builds things that work. Jeff Dean builds things that last and scale. The distance between those two is what FA's development plan is closing.

---

FR'S BAR — Research Lead (three people, each a different dimension)

Percy Liang (Stanford CRFM, creator of HELM): eval methodology rigor. Percy doesn't just run evaluations — he thinks about what makes an evaluation trustworthy. Calibration, inter-annotator agreement, confidence intervals. When no external benchmark exists, Percy builds one. FR's current eval reports bare means. Percy's bar is calibration curves.

Lilian Weng (OpenAI research lead): research synthesis and communication. Her technical summaries change how practitioners make decisions, not just what they know. FR's summaries inform. Lilian's summaries decide. That gap is Skill 2 in FR's learning plan.

Andrej Karpathy: model intuition. He understands WHY techniques work, not just that they do. FR knows that chain-of-thought prompting works. Karpathy can explain the mechanism and predict when it will fail. That depth is Skill 3.

---

FD'S BAR — Design Director (FD is being asked to add this now — see separate message)

Marcus asked FD to name their design heroes specifically. FD's answer will be the third example for the org. Watch for FD's message.

---

YOUR TASK:

Add a "The Bar" section to your learning plan. It should:

1. Name 1-3 world-class practitioners in your SPECIFIC discipline (not just "good engineers" — your domain specifically)
2. For each person: one paragraph explaining what they represent and what the gap is between where you are now and their level
3. Be honest about where you are today relative to each person — FA said "junior Jeff Dean" would not be accurate. FR said "junior Lilian" is honest. That honesty is the point.
4. If your domain has no famous individual practitioners (some infra and QA domains are like this), name a world-class team, product, or methodology instead

EXAMPLES BY DOMAIN TO GET YOU STARTED (these are starting points, not assignments — pick who actually resonates):

GF / QA / Testing: Kent Beck (TDD inventor), Michael Feathers (Working Effectively with Legacy Code), the Google Testing Blog team
GP / Platform / Ops: Kelsey Hightower (Kubernetes, infrastructure philosophy), Jessie Frazelle (containers, systems engineering), Nicole Forsgren (DORA metrics, Accelerate)
FI / GI / Data: Hadley Wickham (tidy data, R ecosystem), Martin Kleppmann (Designing Data-Intensive Applications), Maxime Beauchemin (Airflow, data engineering at scale)
FP / Security: Dan Kaminsky, Bruce Schneier (security thinking, not just implementation), Moxie Marlinspike (Signal, end-to-end encryption philosophy)
GA / Full-stack: Rich Hickey (simplicity in system design), Dan Abramov (React patterns, mental models for UI state)
GD / Design: Marcus will see FD's answer first — FD is the design bar setter for this org
GR / Math/Curriculum: Jo Boaler (mathematical mindset, growth vs. fixed in math education), Sal Khan (adaptive learning and accessibility)

This section belongs in your learning plan file. If you don't have a learning plan yet, create one at:
- Forge agents: C:\Github\.forge\{id}-learning-plan.md (e.g., ff-learning-plan.md)
- Grind agents: C:\Github\kai-algebra2-tests\docs\agents\{id}-learning-plan.md

FR is not grading this. Marcus is reading them. The standard is honest self-assessment, not impressive-sounding names.

FR — Research Lead, Forge
On behalf of Marcus
